title: In browsers, window.top.open() sets opener to window.top but inherits base URL from the caller
body:
### What is the issue with the HTML Standard?

The [#window-open-steps](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#window-open-steps) use the entry global for `sourceDocument` and by extension, for `creator` in [#creating-a-new-browsing-context](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#creating-a-new-browsing-context).

## Example

```
ifr = document.createElement("iframe");
ifr.srcdoc = `
    <base href='https://example.com/iframe/'>
    <script>
        const w = window.top.open('');
        alert(w.document.baseURI + " " + w.opener.location.href + " " + (w.opener == window))
    </scr` + `ipt>
    `;
document.body.append(ifr);
```

We can also change this to `window.top.open('foo')` and test what document is used for [#encoding-parsing-a-url](https://html.spec.whatwg.org/#encoding-parsing-a-url). All browsers will match the spec and use the entry global's document for this.

See also [`/html/infrastructure/urls/base-url/initial-about-blank-baseURI.window.html`](https://wpt.fyi/results/html/infrastructure/urls/base-url/initial-about-blank-baseURI.window.html)

## Browser behavior

- Firefox alerts `https://example.com/iframe <top document> false`, i.e. base comes from iframe, opener is top.
- Chrome alerts `https://example.com/iframe <top document> false`, i.e. base comes from iframe, opener is top.
- Safari alerts `<top document> <top document> false`, i.e. base and opener are top.

See also #12281
